studio.tutorial.pen.title: Sketch with Pen
studio.tutorial.pen.summary: Draw a line directly on the empty canvas and adjust size and opacity.
studio.tutorial.pen.step.1.title: Select the Pen
studio.tutorial.pen.step.1.body: Press B or tap the pen on the bottom tool bar to get ready to draw.
studio.tutorial.pen.step.1.tip: You can switch to eraser instantly by pressing E.
studio.tutorial.pen.step.2.title: Size and opacity
studio.tutorial.pen.step.2.body: Adjust brush size and opacity in drawing options. Use [ ] for quick size changes.
studio.tutorial.pen.step.3.title: Draw naturally
studio.tutorial.pen.step.3.body: After you lift the pen, one stroke is saved. You can undo with ⌘Z anytime.
studio.tutorial.pen.step.3.tip: If shakiness is distracting, raise the stabilization a little.
studio.tutorial.smart-shape.title: Smart Shapes
studio.tutorial.smart-shape.summary: Draw rough lines, rectangles, circles, or triangles and it snaps to clean shapes when you let go.
studio.tutorial.smart-shape.step.1.title: Turn on in Pen Mode
studio.tutorial.smart-shape.step.1.body: Enable Smart Shape in drawing options while the pen tool is selected.
studio.tutorial.smart-shape.step.1.tip: Don't worry about perfection. Just sketch first.
studio.tutorial.smart-shape.step.2.title: Draw like a shape
studio.tutorial.smart-shape.step.2.body: Try drawing a line, rectangle, oval, triangle, or polygon in one stroke. A preview appears when you pause at the end.
studio.tutorial.smart-shape.step.3.title: Release to finalize
studio.tutorial.smart-shape.step.3.body: The stroke snaps to a clean shape right when you release. If it looks off, undo with ⌘Z and try again.
studio.tutorial.smart-shape.step.3.tip: For circles, keep the stroke going to the end; for triangles, make vertices clearly angular for better recognition.
studio.tutorial.brush.title: Brush Kit
studio.tutorial.brush.summary: Change the mood with pen, marker, brush, and highlighter presets.
studio.tutorial.brush.step.1.title: Brush tray
studio.tutorial.brush.step.1.body: Open the brush list in drawing options and choose your preferred texture.
studio.tutorial.brush.step.2.title: Save to slots
studio.tutorial.brush.step.2.body: Save frequent brushes to 1–6 with ⇧, and load them instantly with 1–6.
studio.tutorial.brush.step.3.title: Paint with color
studio.tutorial.brush.step.3.body: Pick a main color and draw. Press X to swap primary and secondary colors.
studio.tutorial.wet-mix.title: Wet-Mix Brush
studio.tutorial.wet-mix.summary: A pigment brush that makes paint look blended as you draw.
studio.tutorial.wet-mix.step.1.title: Enable on image layer
studio.tutorial.wet-mix.step.1.body: Choose an image layer, then click the wet-mix brush or press ⇧N.
studio.tutorial.wet-mix.step.1.tip: You can blend if you flatten a painted stroke into an image first.
studio.tutorial.wet-mix.step.2.title: Paint while mixing
studio.tutorial.wet-mix.step.2.body: The base color sticks to the brush as you paint. Adjust wetness and pigment amount in options.
studio.tutorial.wet-mix.step.3.title: Check stroke-by-stroke
studio.tutorial.wet-mix.step.3.body: Each brush stroke is one undo step. Paint boldly and refine with ⌘Z.
studio.tutorial.dual-brush.title: Dual Brush
studio.tutorial.dual-brush.summary: Combine two brush tips for layered paper and watercolor textures.
studio.tutorial.dual-brush.step.1.title: Open Brush Studio
studio.tutorial.dual-brush.step.1.body: Go to the brush studio from the brush list in drawing options.
studio.tutorial.dual-brush.step.2.title: Enable Dual Brush
studio.tutorial.dual-brush.step.2.body: Turn on dual brush and choose a second tip plus blend mode. The second tip remixes the first texture.
studio.tutorial.dual-brush.step.3.tip: Changing only the blend mode can dramatically shift the look.
studio.tutorial.dual-brush.step.3.title: Preview and save
studio.tutorial.dual-brush.step.3.body: Adjust size and spacing while watching the preview stroke, then save it to a preset.
studio.tutorial.sketch-shape.title: Sketch Shape
studio.tutorial.sketch-shape.summary: Convert geometry into sketchy lines with rough, hand-drawn stroke texture.
studio.tutorial.sketch-shape.step.1.body: Draw a rectangle or oval first, then select the shape object.
studio.tutorial.sketch-shape.step.2.body: In line/shape style, enable sketch-line conversion.
studio.tutorial.sketch-shape.step.3.body: Adjust roughness, bend, and fill texture (like hatching) to match storyboard or doodle style.
studio.tutorial.sketch-shape.step.3.tip: If used in storyboard, enabling this early keeps pressure off feeling incomplete.
studio.tutorial.special-rulers.title: Three Special Rulers
studio.tutorial.special-rulers.summary: Snap guide lines to parallel, concentric, or radial rulers for cleaner backgrounds.
studio.tutorial.special-rulers.step.1.bo: In pen mode, if nothing is selected, add parallel/concentric/radial rulers from drawing options.
studio.tutorial.special-rulers.step.2.bo: Move angle and center point to match the scene. Multiple rulers can display, but only one snaps at a time.
studio.tutorial.special-rulers.step.3.bo: When active, drawn lines snap to guides. Great for rain lines, speed lines, and focus lines.
studio.tutorial.dodge-burn.title: Dodge/Burn/Sponge
studio.tutorial.dodge-burn.summary: Use brush strokes to subtly adjust brightness and color saturation.
studio.tutorial.dodge-burn.step.1.title: Turn on in image mode
studio.tutorial.dodge-burn.step.1.body: Select an image layer to adjust and tap dodge/burn, or press O.
studio.tutorial.dodge-burn.step.2.title: Choose mode
studio.tutorial.dodge-burn.step.2.body: Dodge brightens, burn darkens, and sponge raises or lowers saturation. You can also choose range: shadow/midtone/highlight.
studio.tutorial.dodge-burn.step.3.title: Go lightly, multiple passes
studio.tutorial.dodge-burn.step.3.body: Lower exposure and do many passes for smoother results. Each stroke is one undo step.
studio.tutorial.dodge-burn.step.3.tip: Start with narrow areas first, like skin highlights and rim light.
studio.tutorial.quick-mask.title: Quick Mask
studio.tutorial.quick-mask.summary: Paint mask areas with a brush, then refine selected regions like Photoshop's Q mode.
studio.tutorial.quick-mask.step.1.title: Enter with Q
studio.tutorial.quick-mask.step.1.body: Choose an image layer and press Q. Current pixel selection changes into a color mask overlay.
studio.tutorial.quick-mask.step.1.tip: You can also start from the quick mask panel in the Dialogue/Retouch tab.
studio.tutorial.quick-mask.step.2.title: Paint to refine
studio.tutorial.quick-mask.step.2.body: Brush adds selection to the painted area, and erase removes it. One press also inverts the entire mask.
studio.tutorial.quick-mask.step.3.title: Finish to selection
studio.tutorial.quick-mask.step.3.body: Press Q again to convert the refined mask back to pixel selection. Soft edges keep feathering automatically.
studio.tutorial.color-range.title: Color Range Selection
studio.tutorial.color-range.summary: Select regions by picking similar colors at once.
studio.tutorial.color-range.step.1.title: Open Selection/Retouch
studio.tutorial.color-range.step.1.body: Select an image layer and open the Color Range section in the Selection/Retouch tab.
studio.tutorial.color-range.step.2.title: Base color and tolerance
studio.tutorial.color-range.step.2.body: Pick a target color and adjust tolerance to see the preview coverage.
studio.tutorial.color-range.step.3.title: Apply selection
studio.tutorial.color-range.step.3.body: The selection is applied by current combine mode: New, Merge, or Subtract. Then you can adjust colors or delete.
studio.tutorial.color-range.step.3.tip: Especially useful for areas with clear boundaries, like sky or hair.
studio.tutorial.bubble.title: Speech Bubbles
studio.tutorial.bubble.summary: Choose a bubble style that fits the scene: speech, thought, and shout tones.
studio.tutorial.bubble.step.1.title: Choose bubble type
studio.tutorial.bubble.step.1.body: Use the top bubble menu to choose from speech, emotion, and staging UI groups.
studio.tutorial.bubble.step.1.tip: You can still fine-tune shape in the right-side property panel.
studio.tutorial.bubble.step.2.title: Input dialogue
studio.tutorial.bubble.step.2.body: Double-click/tap a bubble on the canvas to edit text. Color, tail, and mood can be changed from properties after selection.
studio.tutorial.bubble.step.3.title: Mood swatch
studio.tutorial.bubble.step.3.body: Use the mood swatch in properties to balance color, stroke, and shape at once.
studio.tutorial.dialogue.title: Batch Dialogue Input
studio.tutorial.dialogue.summary: Paste a script and bubbles are generated in sequence automatically.
studio.tutorial.dialogue.step.1.title: Script format
studio.tutorial.dialogue.step.1.body: Use one line per dialogue. Name and line format (Name: Dialogue) creates speaker separation; (Narration) makes narration boxes.
studio.tutorial.dialogue.step.2.title: Insert all at once
studio.tutorial.dialogue.step.2.body: Paste into the input area below bubble menu and click Insert All Bubbles.
studio.tutorial.dialogue.step.3.title: Batch editing
studio.tutorial.dialogue.step.3.body: Use batch dialogue editing to revise all pasted text together.
studio.tutorial.template.title: Cut Templates
studio.tutorial.template.summary: Set up layout quickly with vertical webtoon, 4-panel, or grid setups.
studio.tutorial.template.step.1.title: Choose a template
studio.tutorial.template.step.1.body: Pick a vertical webtoon, grid, or other layout from template links.
studio.tutorial.template.step.2.title: Draw in frames
studio.tutorial.template.step.2.body: Put drawings, bubbles, and characters inside each frame. Frames structure scene flow.
studio.tutorial.template.step.3.title: Adjust dimensions
studio.tutorial.template.step.3.body: You can resize by canvas height or by each frame. For vertical scrolling webtoons, longer lengths usually work better.
studio.tutorial.layers.title: Layers & Selection
studio.tutorial.layers.summary: Sort elements by layering, visibility, and lock state.
studio.tutorial.layers.step.1.title: Select an element
studio.tutorial.layers.step.1.body: Tap an element with selection tool to highlight it in properties and layer list.
studio.tutorial.layers.step.2.title: Reorder layers
studio.tutorial.layers.step.2.body: Drag in the layer list or use ⌘] / ⌘[ to move forward/back.
studio.tutorial.layers.step.3.title: Hide or lock
studio.tutorial.layers.step.3.body: Hide or lock distracting elements so they don't move during edits.
studio.tutorial.layers.step.3.tip: Use arrow keys for 1px move, and ⇧+arrow keys for 10px move.
studio.tutorial.path-boolean.title: Path Boolean
studio.tutorial.path-boolean.summary: Combine, subtract, intersect, and split two shapes into one clean path.
studio.tutorial.path-boolean.step.1.body: Select two shapes to combine using drag or Shift+click.
studio.tutorial.path-boolean.step.2.body: In Shape Combine, choose Union, Subtract, Intersect, or Split.
studio.tutorial.path-boolean.step.3.body: The merged shape becomes one path. If needed, undo with ⌘Z and try again.
studio.tutorial.path-boolean.step.3.tip: Useful for complex bubble silhouettes and signs.
studio.tutorial.character.title: 3D Character
studio.tutorial.character.summary: Set up pose, clothing, and props for a scene with a VRM character.
studio.tutorial.character.step.1.title: Add character
studio.tutorial.character.step.1.body: Place a model or preset from the character menu onto the canvas.
studio.tutorial.character.step.2.title: Pose setup
studio.tutorial.character.step.2.body: Use pose presets or joint manipulation to match intended motion.
studio.tutorial.character.step.3.title: Costume and props
studio.tutorial.character.step.3.body: Use wardrobe and prop libraries to add atmosphere. If it looks awkward, make tiny micro adjustments.
studio.tutorial.bg3d.title: 3D Background
studio.tutorial.bg3d.summary: Quickly block in a room, street, or set with scene templates.
studio.tutorial.bg3d.step.1.title: Scene template
studio.tutorial.bg3d.step.1.body: Select a room or street template in 3D background and place it at once.
studio.tutorial.bg3d.step.2.title: Place objects
studio.tutorial.bg3d.step.2.body: Move furniture and props, then snap to floor guides. You can also hide and lock layers.
studio.tutorial.bg3d.step.3.title: Camera feel
studio.tutorial.bg3d.step.3.body: Adjust camera angle and light to quickly set the scene tone.
studio.tutorial.mannequin.title: 3D Figure
studio.tutorial.mannequin.summary: Use a pose figure to define anatomy scaffolding for your scene.
studio.tutorial.mannequin.step.1.title: Open Figure
studio.tutorial.mannequin.step.1.body: Open the figure tool in the main toolbar. Rotation/zoom behaves like 3D Character controls.
studio.tutorial.mannequin.step.2.title: Pose it
studio.tutorial.mannequin.step.2.body: Create motion by dragging joints or starting from pose presets. You can also adjust proportions with sliders.
studio.tutorial.mannequin.step.3.title: Insert as sketch
studio.tutorial.mannequin.step.3.body: After inserting, lower opacity and sketch lines over it to make an anatomy guide.
studio.tutorial.mannequin.step.3.tip: For difficult angles, rotate the figure first before drawing.
studio.tutorial.room-builder.title: Room Builder
studio.tutorial.room-builder.summary: Quickly block out room geometry by changing measurements.
studio.tutorial.room-builder.step.1.body: Choose Room Builder in 3D background. A base room with floor and walls is prepared.
studio.tutorial.room-builder.step.2.body: Adjust width, depth, height, and door/window positions. Changes instantly rebuild the room.
studio.tutorial.room-builder.step.3.body: Add it to scene to place furniture and props. Time-of-day mood can be tuned with sun rig and lights.
studio.tutorial.ai-assist.title: AI Assist
studio.tutorial.ai-assist.summary: Use dialogue suggestions and rewrites to unblock difficult scenes.
studio.tutorial.ai-assist.step.1.title: Open hub
studio.tutorial.ai-assist.step.1.body: In AI Assist menu, pick the tool tab you need.
studio.tutorial.ai-assist.step.2.title: Add context
studio.tutorial.ai-assist.step.2.body: Add scene, speaker, and tone briefly for better suggestions. Edit results rather than inserting as-is.
studio.tutorial.ai-assist.step.2.tip: Some functions may require your own BYOK API key.
studio.tutorial.ai-assist.step.3.title: Apply to canvas
studio.tutorial.ai-assist.step.3.body: Insert preferred lines into bubbles or apply via the Apply button.
studio.tutorial.export.title: Export
studio.tutorial.export.summary: Save and share your work with PNG, JSON backups, and more.
studio.tutorial.export.step.1.title: Save as image
studio.tutorial.export.step.1.body: Choose image scale in the top Download menu (e.g., 2× PNG) and save.
studio.tutorial.export.step.2.title: Backup project
studio.tutorial.export.step.2.body: JSON backup stores layers and bubbles together. Reload it later when you return.
studio.tutorial.export.step.3.title: Final check
studio.tutorial.export.step.3.body: Before publish/upload, review once more and export only selected cuts if needed.
studio.tutorial.gif-export.title: GIF/APNG Export
studio.tutorial.gif-export.summary: Save frame animation as a playable animation file anywhere.
studio.tutorial.gif-export.step.1.title: Create frames
studio.tutorial.gif-export.step.1.body: Choose image layers and stack frames in Frame Animation panel to build a short animation.
studio.tutorial.gif-export.step.2.title: Choose format
studio.tutorial.gif-export.step.2.body: Select GIF or APNG. GIF plays almost everywhere; APNG usually preserves quality better.
studio.tutorial.gif-export.step.3.title: Save and share
studio.tutorial.gif-export.step.3.body: After setting speed and repeats, save to share an animation-ready file immediately.
studio.tutorial.gif-export.step.3.tip: Use GIF for community uploads and APNG for higher-quality exports.
